newsitem.title: UK: EMU could cost UK retailers 3.5 billion stg - BRC.
newsitem.headline: EMU could cost UK retailers 3.5 billion stg - BRC.

text.p: A single European currency could cost UK retailers up to 3.5 billion stg if Britain signs up, the British Retail Consortium (BRC) said on Tuesday.
Costs include staff training, re-labelling and adjusting operating and point of sales systems to handle the new currency, said the BRC report.

The BRC estimated an added indirect cost of 300 million stg from changes to the pricing of products and the impact on trading patterns where shoppers would be expected to buy more before the change over and less immediately after.

But these costs could be cut to 1.7 billion stg if a number proposals were followed. Among the BRC's suggestions for cuttting costs are: -- if EMU was launched in a quiet trading period, ideally February. January 1 is one of the busiest times of the year -- the euro should be introduced in one go as opposed to running two currencies side by side -- price labelling should be determined by individual retailers -- retailers need a least three years advance notice before switching currency

Alastair Eperon, director of the BRC, said retailers had the front line responsibility for insuring the successful introduction of a single currency if that is the course the government decides to pursue.

"The practical implications are huge and the costs significant, but this research shows that there are easy ways in which the process of introduction can be simplified to the benefit of consumers and retailers alike."
